deep.reconstruction:
Setting. f(z)=∏_{i≥1}(1+α_i z) is an entire function given by a convergent product without exponential factors, so ∑|α_i|<∞. Put F(z)=∏(1+|α_i| z). Claim: f and F have the same order ρ, so the order depends only on the moduli |α_i|.

Proof sketch on the page:
- ord f ≤ ord F, because |f(z)| ≤ F(|z|) and M_f(r) ≤ F(r).
- ord F equals the exponent of convergence of the sequence (|α_i|), i.e. inf{s>0 : ∑|α_i|^s<∞}. This is Borel's theorem for canonical products of genus 0. The 'voir ci-dessous' points to the next page, which proves ∑ r_ν^{-α}<∞ ⇔ ∫ n(r) r^{-α-1} dr<∞ by Stieltjes integration by parts with the counting function n(r). The previous page had already checked the case α_n = n^{-β}, giving order 1/β.
- The exponent of convergence of the zeros (−1/α_i) is ≤ ord f, by Hadamard.
Hence equality.

Abstraction. One may therefore speak of the 'order' of a countable family of complex numbers: inf{s>0 : ∑|z_i|^s<∞}. The order of a sequence tending to 0 is ≥0, and it is 0 exactly when ∑|z_i|^s<∞ for all s>0, i.e. (after decreasing rearrangement) the sequence is rapidly decreasing.

Generalisation to functional analysis:
- Orders of a sequence in a Banach or Fréchet space, with several definitions: weak s-summability (∑|⟨x',x_i⟩|^s<∞ for all x') or absolute summability (∑‖x_i‖^s<∞, seminorm by seminorm).
- Order of a bounded set: the infimum of s such that the set lies in the closed (absolutely) convex hull of a sequence of order s.

Purpose. This is groundwork for Grothendieck's theory of s-nuclear / order-s operators and nuclear spaces (Produits tensoriels topologiques). It also prepares the Fredholm theory, where the Fredholm determinant det(1+zu) is an entire function whose order is controlled by the summability exponent of the operator and of its eigenvalues.
errors: The product ∏(1+α_i z) without convergence factors converges iff ∑|α_i|<∞. The function is then a canonical product of genus 0 (order ≤1), so 'de genre 1' is either a slip or means order/genus ≤ 1.

The step 'ord F = order of the sequence (|α_i|)' is Borel's theorem on canonical products. It is not proved on this page; it is deferred to the next page's integration-by-parts lemma, which alone gives only the n(r) criterion, not the growth estimate for F.

The definition inf{s>0: ∑|z_i|^s<∞} is meaningful only for sequences tending to 0, i.e. countable sets with no accumulation except 0. The equivalence order zero ⇔ rapid decrease requires rearranging in decreasing order.

ideas.what: Order of a genus-0 canonical product equals exponent of convergence of its zeros and depends only on their moduli
ideas.modern_name: Borel's theorem / Hadamard factorization; exponent of convergence
ideas.where_published: Used implicitly in 'La théorie de Fredholm' (Bull. SMF 1956) for Fredholm determinants

ideas.what: Order of a sequence of complex numbers = inf{s: ∑|z_i|^s<∞}; order zero = rapidly decreasing

ideas.usually_credited_to: classical; used systematically by Grothendieck (PTT 1955), Pietsch
ideas.where_published: Produits tensoriels topologiques et espaces nucléaires (Mem. AMS 16, 1955), Ch. II

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft working out the classical link between order of entire functions and summability exponents, then abstracting it to orders of sequences and bounded sets in Banach/Fréchet spaces. That is precisely the motivation behind the s-nuclear operators of PTT and the 1956 Fredholm paper, both published. It is nice to see the entire-function origin of the term 'ordre', but nothing here is absent from the literature.
